note: The Handover's route scripts (brief 011 B, Waymark), played headless by the mission checker (bun run missions:check handover). Rewritten 2026-10-15 for Keel's round-2 engine: the final fight (N10, N11) and the crowd are on in every script, the cast is M-2's from the promoted people run r016 (sim/data/handover.site.json cast, 2026-10-16; Inez p-cafe-14 Fearful, the guard p-records-office-01, the driver p-records-office-31 and Vale p-records-office-07 Mercenary), so route A helps Inez twice (§04: a Fearful person needs Help ×2), Watch takes 20 s and the fight's shots are untraced (Sky's balance rulings). The scripts start from Keel's scenarios where one exists (N10, N11, N11b, S09, S25, N08), without their fixtures and keeping only the orders the engine took; every fixture a script would need became orders. Keel's readings are kept: the response unit enters from the north street (§07 'west street'), one door guard stays the whole mission, and Vale follows the mission's timeline, not his routine. Closing events (Suture's question; Aster 2026-10-15): route A's is Vale's exit at 5:50 (§07 route A, before 5:50), secured when the Enforcer is inside; route B's is the mission's close, 8:30 since Sky's ruling (rivals take Vale or the car leaves), secured when Vale is with the Enforcer. A carry in progress at the close (Waymark's ruling, 2026-10-15, on Keel's E8): the close ends the take, not a carry already under way. If the Enforcer holds Vale at 8:30 the run goes on (the engine logs horizon.open) and wins only when Vale reaches the getaway car; the final fight, the seal and the Enforcer's health bound the carry. Recommended to Keel and Motive, not yet in the engine: a hard stop at 12:00 (§01: a mission is 8-12 min) where a carry still under way ends as 'district seals'. Brief 013 D (Waymark, 2026-10-16): the takedown engine (Keel 0.5.0, security level 2, the guard's check-in marks every 90 s). Route G takes the guard out (knockout; fast; kill hidden behind the service door). Careless scripts (kind careless) do the same violence seen by a camera, seen by a crowd, found before the exit, or reported unstopped, each against its careful twin (MC-7). Trail is compared in total, the mission's plus what the debrief carries into the campaign. Rev 4 (2026-10-16): a found body holds the doors in its sight (careless-guard-left-door-held); open cases are priced at the rulebook's case-trail-eq in the totals. The driver route (Motive §6.2) is still not scripted: with the pickup loop and three bodies to a service door it plays, but each staff victim's missed mark is its own incident (the second lands at Alert 2, and the search opens the service door), and every witness at the bay tells a Loyal workmate by telephone (briefs/013/waymark-handover.md §5). Brief 018 (Waymark, 2026-10-18; Keel's engine 0.7.0, the getaway): extract is retired into Board and Go. Each quiet route has two references: fight it out (the original id: the Enforcer waits for the crew to break, boards, and the car leaves; the three walk out) and board and go (<id>-board, the primary of A, B and G: the Enforcer walks Vale to the car as the ambush springs, the three board once the blocker is down, nobody left behind). Loud has board and go (loud), fight it out (loud-fight) and the cheapest (loud-fast), each boarding the whole cell, since the seal clock captures anyone left standing. loud-left-downed and loud-left-standing are the two runs that leave an op behind (captured downed; captured fighting, abandoned). Plans may wait for the engine's `blocker.out` (c019: the engine logs it, and `car.free`). c019 (engine 0.7.x: walking Vale, the Enforcer does not fire): plans recomposed; loud-fast keeps its cover and carries its downed Fixer in. MC-10 checks quiet beats loud on Trail (a captive's +4 T counts as campaign Trail), Alert, Standing and the seal; MC-11 that no ambush spot or police stand holds the car. Brief 031 (Waymark, 2026-10-20; Keel's engine 0.11.0: every agent Watches at its own reach, and security watchers notice loiterers: a clock per watcher and agent, running while the agent stands still in its sight, noticed at 8 s, wary at 20 s, reported at 45 s at the Handover's Heat 0, mission.json start.heat): every quiet and loud route's waits are re-sited out of sight, so no watcher that keeps a clock sees an agent stand. The Enforcer waits on the forecourt (56.5, -47.5), behind the entrance camera's cone and the patrol's sweep and outside the guard's, and goes to the door's south side only once the patrol has left (A, loud) or walks in for the blow (G); in route B the Scout watches the driver from the Office's south-west corner and waits for the tip 2.8 m outside the pickup camera's cone, and the Fixer walks to the driver as the Watch ends; in route G the Scout watches the guard from 27.4 m, beyond his cone. A Watch in reach starts where the agent stands, so a Watch step waits (gap) for the walk to its spot. Every script states the Alert it ends at (expects.alert); MC-12 checks that no quiet script is reported for loitering and that the careless-loiter twin costs more than its careful twin. The fail scripts keep their fail codes; where a careless player's agent stands in a camera's view, it is now reported (Alert 1), which they keep. Brief 055 (Waymark, 2026-10-24; Keel's engine 0.27.0: the four Office-front cypresses are walk solids): the Enforcer's wait beside the public door, (69.5, -42.5), fell inside cyp-office-w's body clearance, so the move there was refused and the Enter after it failed; it is re-sited to (69.25, -42.5), the free cell beside it on the street (the scenarios' BesideDoor), in route A and its twin, the five loud plans, and the seven hand scripts that stand there (careless-body-found, careless-takedown-seen-camera, careless-takedown-seen-crowd, fail-district-seals, fail-entry-seen-camera, -guard, -patrol). Route G-kill's stash is re-composed (3:07.1, the carry round the cypresses is longer). Brief 056 (Waymark, 2026-10-24; Keel's engine 0.28.0: sight from real heights, the drawn walk grid and occluders, civilians who see by a cone and below Alert 2 care only about violence, and a Watch offered only where it shows something): every plan re-composed. The driver shows no mood (a Mercenary at fear 0), so no Watch on her is offered and Listen and Pay need none: the Scout's Watch of the driver is dropped from route-b, -board, -block, -block-board, careless-reporter-not-stopped and careless-scout-idles-pickup (and from the hand scripts fail-rivals-reach-vale and fight-safe-rivals-reach-vale, where it was refused); the Scout and the Fixer go on from the corner to the driver once there, about 20 s sooner. On the drawn walk the board-and-go Scout's cover by the car's east end (1175, -4825) is in rival-3's line as he walks to board, and he is downed short of the car: route-g-board, -g-fast-board, -g-kill-board and -a-pressure-board now cover from the car's north-west corner (725, -4625, cv-003), route G's own post (route-a-board, route-b-board and route-b-block-board still board from the east end). careless-reporter-not-stopped and careless-scout-idles-pickup take route-b's final-fight posts, so each differs from its twin only in its mistake. A guard's sight is watched once, so careless-enforcer-watches-guard drops the Scout's Watch and the Enforcer's from 3 m is the only one. The mission's cameras name their kind (pole-camera, the lens height the rulebook's perception.mount reads). Fight-it-out wins end 8-11 s later than on 0.27.0 (the crew takes longer to break on the drawn ground); board-and-go wins within 0.3 s. Brief 058 (Waymark, 2026-10-25; Keel's engine 0.31.0, Loop v2: a loop lands 20 s after it is ordered and runs 2:00 from the landing on its own, with no tether; Disable cuts a camera for good, +2 T, and the desk's report of the dead screen is an incident): every route that loops is re-timed so its loop still runs at the act it covers. Route A and its board twin plant the loop at 1:25 (live 1:45 to 3:45) and reroute as it lands (the patrol away 2:30 to 4:25): rerouting first, as brief 058 §6 suggested, brings the patrol back at 2:56.5, 3 s after the Enter, where this order keeps c036's slack (7 s, the Inez limit; 51 s from the wait by the door); the loud family plants at 1:00 (live 1:20 to 3:20) and reroutes as it lands (patrol away 2:05 to 4:00, as c036); route G and its twin plant at 1:00 (live 1:20 to 3:20); route G-kill and its twin reroute at 1:25, not 1:46, and plant the loop as the patrol leaves (2:10, live 2:30 to 4:30: it lands before the 2:31 kill and still runs at the 4:04 Enter); A-pressure and G-fast keep their order (loop first, then Reroute) and, recomposed, run faster, since the loop now holds the Tech 20 s, not 62 s: A-pressure-board 3:38.1 to 3:20.5, G-fast-board 3:53 to 3:11, same Trail, Alert and Standing. Every re-timed route keeps c036's end, Trail, Alert and Standing. fail-entry-seen-patrol plants its loop at 2:40 and walks the Enforcer to the door as it lands; careless-guard-left-door-held's mistake is now the Enforcer dawdling a minute after the blow (the Tech walking off no longer ends a loop): the loop runs out with the guard at the door and the unit holds it. careless-takedown-seen-crowd is re-sited to 5:30.0, when the clerks leaving face the door, so a civilian reports it (brief 054 §6), with the Enforcer waiting on the forecourt and the loop planted at 4:20. New: route-a-disable (route A with Disable in place of the Loop: 6 T, Alert 1, a quiet win counted under A), careless-g-disable (route G with Disable: the guard's missed 4:00 mark becomes the second incident, Alert 2 in the final fight, security joins it and the three are captured) and careless-loop-runs-out (route A with the loop planted first: it runs out before the Enter, entry-seen-camera; careless fault timing).

scripts.src: brief 031 §7 (Waymark 4); Sky 2026-10-20 D1 (being seen watching makes the target wary)
scripts.note: Route-g-fast, but the Enforcer watches the guard himself from his side before the knockout: the guard senses him within 3 m, the Watch runs his clock to wary, and a wary guard is aware at the blow: he draws, the takedown fails, and the Enforcer goes down. Engine 0.28.0 (brief 054 §2.1): a guard's sight and marks are watched once, so the Scout no longer watches him first; the Enforcer's Watch from his side is the only one: noticed 2:20.1, wary 2:32.1, the blow at 2:32.5 fails, Enforcer down 3:35.1.

scripts.src: brief 031 §7 (Waymark 4)
scripts.note: Route-b, but the Scout waits for the 3:10 tip in the pickup camera's view: reported as a loiterer at its desk's next scan (Alert 1, the dial's two robots, no Trail); the route still wins, one Alert dearer than its twin (A 0). Engine 0.28.0: route-b's final-fight posts (the Scout at cv-003, the Fixer at cv-002), so it differs from route-b only in its mistake; ends with route-b at 8:07.9.

scripts.src: brief 058 §4, §6 (Disable is worse on every G route)
scripts.note: Route G with Disable in place of the Loop, landing when route-g's loop does: the desk's report of the dead screen is the first incident (Alert 1), the guard knocked out at 2:31 misses his 4:00 mark, and that second incident lifts the run to Alert 2 during the final fight; security joins it, the Fixer is downed, and when the car leaves the three who would have walked out on a calm street are captured (+4 T each into the campaign).

scripts.src: brief 058 §6 (Loop v2: a loop runs 2:00 from its landing)
scripts.note: Route A with the loop planted first, as soon as the Tech reaches the cabinet (live 0:36.5 to 2:36.5): it runs out 17 s before the Enter, and the entrance camera sees it.
